scope: Independent read-only final proposal3 source/native-contract/ABI/early-install/diagnostics/test review. No build, GPU, runtime, UI or shared source mutation.
findings: Actual supported66d PE bytes independently match all complete failed caller, MIDI close, MIDI plugin-delete wrapper and module unload contracts. Only failed-Wave unload callsite0x5f9b7d is redirected.

Native thiscall MIDI close receives ECX=0xcaaad8 via existing fastcall adapter with no stack arguments. Native unload is argument-free cdecl. Rust C hook preserves nonvolatile ESI, and actual native caller restores its original Wave error from ESI after redirected cleanup. Hook forwards original unload return without substituting close result.

MIDI close runs before original module unload on original failure thread, using existing native backend shutdown/plugin delete/pointer clearing. No direct child pointer writes, forced startup success, global FreeLibrary interception, normal success/shutdown callsite patch, audio clock or pitch change.

Early install uses supported absolute base/build, zero initialized/module/three-backend/eleven-factory preinit reads and full native code contracts before callsite patch. Active/stale/unreadable late state declines without dereferencing backend objects.

DllMain addition uses bounded guarded reads, at most small fixed successful hook allocations and existing code protection/write/cache-flush machinery. No new library load, file IO, GUI, sound call, explicit waiting lock, retry, new thread or audio call occurs there. Existing init-thread status logging occurs later.

Proposal3 trace output is a # comment and only calls diagnostics while servicing the existing trace request. Diagnostics reads guarded globals, not child vtables or unloaded code; unsupported/declined states perform no native-global reads. Healthy audio per-frame paths gain no polling/logging.

Immutable first claimed completed close/unload results are published behind first_ready Release/Acquire. Snapshot reads readiness before count; readiness false yields explicit None even if a completed-count increment is visible. Later unwind completions never overwrite that pair, so repeated/nested calls cannot expose results mixed across completions. No spin or wait added.

Twelve prepared tests cover native-lifetime/order regression and absent-MIDI behavior, original cleanup result preservation, supported-image/base and stale/unreadable gate rejection, native-code mismatch gate, actual caller/ABI/error-restoration bytes, publish-after-both-calls evidence, retained nested/late first-completion record, and requested diagnostics states. These are meaningful unit/static tests, not claimed execution evidence.
limits: Proposal3 has no compiler or runtime evidence at this review. Prior source1 evidence cannot qualify these metadata changes or final PE identity. Exact final CPU tests/Windows ABI compile and causal failure plus normal loaded-game lifecycle acceptance remain required before runtime promotion.

On-demand initialized/module/backend/factory values are independent guarded reads, not one atomic native-state snapshot. Retained first completion results have coherent publication; current native fields must not be interpreted as transactional proof of simultaneous state.

The first record is selected by the first successful claim after both native calls finish. The real intercepted path is the original game thread; the nested completion test validates completion order under reentry. No stronger cross-thread chronological selection is claimed.
decision: No blocking source issue found in final proposal3. Suitable for authorized isolated compile/tests and exact runtime qualification. No shipping/runtime/performance acceptance.
